title: Registry: mergedObjectCache is not dropped when an enabled package record is installed or removed, so a fold that reads package records can go stale
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

Filed as a `finding` by seat `repo:objectstack#2` from l2-review#4 record 7085456800 on PR #36517 (nit N3). Not triaged; not claimed.

## What

After PR #36517, the registry's object fold reads the installed package records: the `.custom` arrangement asks `pairsOf(owner, installed manifests)`. On `main`, the placement step already does the same thing (`childPackageOf` reads other objects' owners at fold time).

`mergedObjectCache` is dropped when an object registration changes, or when a package is enabled or disabled. It is **not** dropped when an enabled package's record is installed or removed. Suppose an object's fold is cached after the pair's extension is registered but before the App's record arrives (or before a record in the owner's dependency chain). Then the cached answer skips the App's pair, and the boot log names it as "not the customization package". This lasts until the next registration on that object, or the next enable or disable.

L2 could not show by reading the code that this order is reachable. The engine installs each package's record before its contributions, and a member declaring its App in `dependencies` should register after it. No suite pins the order, though. If any load order reaches it, it is a real defect: a declared arrangement would not be applied.

## Ask

Either drop the cache when a package record is installed or removed, or pin the order with a test that fails if it is ever reversed.

## Likely lane

`domain:server` (`packages/objectql/src/registry*.ts`).

## Re-check

`grep -n "mergedObjectCache" packages/objectql/src/*.ts`: check whether any package-record install or remove path clears it.
